gap: No result ChatGPT got cites a maker document on how a station's neutral is wired. Jackery's own HomePower 3000 (JE-3000B) spec FAQ answers the question 'is the neutral floating or bonded?' with 'floating', and the same FAQ calls its 120V/30A TT-30 port 'an auxiliary power input for small camper vans and trailers'. That matters for a trailer with a hardwired EMS or surge protector that checks for a missing ground.
standout_why: I compared against both cited rivals and the top result. quiettechreport.com (cited) already warns under the HomePower 3000 that 'floating-neutral arrangements may trigger an EMS/open-ground fault', but it doesn't cite Jackery and says 'may'. solutionenergy.com (cited) gives each model's TT-30 amp rating (C2000 Gen 2 20 A, HomePower 3000 30 A, DELTA Pro 3 'true 30 A') and the expansion batteries, and says Jackery requires a 'grounding adapter'. It never says whether any neutral is floating or bonded. Neither page names a maker's statement on a specific model's neutral, so our page would add the source and the certainty, not a new idea.
decides: This doesn't change the pick. It confirms that the trailer's EMS should be checked before buying. Jackery documents the HomePower 3000 (ChatGPT's 'best balance' pick) as floating neutral and not expandable ('battery packs: Not supported'). An owner whose hardwired EMS checks for a ground should expect an open-ground fault, and Jackery offers no expansion path. For the Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 (ChatGPT's #1), Anker's page puts the TT-30R at 20 A / 2,400 W. That is below the 30 A the trailer's inlet implies, even though Anker's headline says 'Power Your Entire RV' and claims the unit runs 'most window and RV A/Cs'.

findings.label: Neutral wiring
findings.source_title: HomePower 3000 Basic Information (Jackery FAQ, model JE-3000B, updated 2026-08-19)
findings.note: This is Jackery's own answer to 'is the neutral wire floating or bonded'. A trailer EMS or surge protector that checks for a ground may report open ground. Jackery's FAQ doesn't mention a bonding plug or adapter for this model.

findings.label: TT-30 output and shared AC limit
findings.value: TT-30 120 V / 30 A; 4 × 120 V 20 A outlets + 1 × 120 V 30 A; 3,600 W total across the 5 ports; 7,200 W instantaneous
findings.note: Jackery lists the RV use as 'auxiliary power input for small camper vans and trailers'. The 50 A port entry is blank ('/'), so there's no 50 A output. The 3,600 W limit is shared by all five ports, so other AC loads cut what the TT-30 can deliver.

findings.label: Expansion, parallel and car charging
findings.value: expansion battery packs not supported; parallel not supported; car fast charger about 5.6 h; car port about 36 h at 11–16 V, 8 A
findings.note: The FAQ doesn't mention an alternator charger. UPS switchover is within 20 ms, and Jackery says this is 'not a 0 ms' UPS.

findings.label: TT-30R rating
findings.value: 120 V, 20 A max, 2,400 W max (4,000 W peak)
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 product page
findings.note: 20 A × 120 V = 2,400 W, which is two-thirds of a 30 A (3,600 W) trailer inlet. On the same page Anker headlines 'Power Your Entire RV via TT-30 Port' and says it runs 'most window and RV A/Cs'.

findings.label: Compatible expansion battery and alternator charging
findings.value: Anker SOLIX BP2000 Expansion Battery (Gen 2) only, 2,048 Wh, up to 4 kWh total; alternator charging up to 800 W (to 100% in 3 h per Anker)
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 product page
findings.note: FAQ Q4 names only the BP2000 (Gen 2). The comparison table marks alternator charging 'Not Supported' on the F2000. The AC input is listed as L+N+PE, but the page says nothing about the neutral-ground state of the outputs.

findings.label: Extra battery link cable compatibility
findings.value: Extra Battery Flat Link Cable connects DELTA Pro 3 to the DELTA Pro 3 Smart Extra Battery or the DELTA Pro Extra Battery; $89.00; 0.85 m or 2 m
findings.source_title: EcoFlow Extra Battery Flat Link Cable (EcoFlow US store)
findings.note: Read with storecheck.py. EcoFlow notes this cable's design 'is different from that of the DELTA Pro Extra Battery Cable', so the older DELTA Pro cable doesn't carry over.

findings.label: Alternator charger compatibility
findings.value: EcoFlow 500W Alternator Charger $199.00; reverse charging and battery maintenance only with the XT150 cable on DELTA-series units; the original DELTA Pro (not Pro 3) needs a DELTA Pro to Smart Generator Adapter
findings.note: Read with storecheck.py. The included XT60 cable charges only. Used with third-party stations, it doesn't support reverse charging or battery maintenance.

findings.label: Cross-generation extra battery compatibility
findings.value: DELTA 3: DELTA 3, DELTA Pro 3, DELTA 2 or DELTA 2 Max Extra Battery (1–5 kWh). DELTA 3800 Gen4: DELTA Pro 3 Smart Extra Battery and DELTA 3 Max Plus (2,048 Wh) Smart Extra Battery (4–12 kWh)
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Portable Power Station (EcoFlow US store search result)
findings.note: The DELTA 3800 Gen4 line comes from https://us.ecoflow.com/products/delta-3800-gen4, read the same day through storecheck.py search.

findings.label: Which BLUETTI models have a native TT-30
findings.value: AC200L and Elite 300 only, as named by BLUETTI; both listed at 2,400 W
findings.source_title: What Is a TT-30 Outlet? RV 30 Amp Plug Explained (2026 Guide), BLUETTI, 2026-10-05
findings.note: BLUETTI calls both 'true TT-30 plug-and-play' but gives no amp rating per outlet. 2,400 W ÷ 120 V = 20 A of inverter output on a 30 A receptacle. The article doesn't address neutral bonding or EMS open-ground faults.
